aperiodicity_theorem.multiple_construction: for odd k>bit_length(p), d=p(2^k-1) has odd binary digit sum and is a multiple of p
aperiodicity_theorem.orbit_closure_argument: a p-periodic point in X_TM would contribute such a forbidden p-periodic window to the Thue--Morse language
aperiodicity_theorem.popcount_identity: popcount(p(2^k-1))=k because p(2^k-1)=(p-1)2^k+(2^k-p) and the low k bits are the complement of p-1
aperiodicity_theorem.window_argument: every interval of length 2^(b+1) contains a complete b-aligned block; its offsets 0 and d differ but are congruent modulo p

language_prefix.language_capture: for 2^q>=m, every length-m factor lies in one of the four concatenations w_qw_q, w_q complement(w_q), complement(w_q)w_q, complement(w_q)complement(w_q)

nonclaims: that periodic approximants belong to X_TM
that absence of periodic points implies absence of invariant measures or recurrence
an arithmetic Euler product or local factorization
a target divisor, functional equation, or counting-law match
Route-B authorization or a solution of the larger program

periodic_approximants.definition: c_k is the bi-infinite repetition of w_k=t_[0,2^k)
periodic_approximants.seam_bound: for a width-m window with m<=2^k, only the m-1 seam-crossing starts can be extrinsic, so the invalid rooted fraction is at most (m-1)/2^k
periodic_approximants.stress_control: for 2<=k<=9 every rooted window of width 2^(k+1)+1 in c_k is absent from the intrinsic language; this is an exact finite ledger, not an all-k theorem
periodic_approximants.warning: c_k is a finite periodic control and is not a point of X_TM

progress_and_boundary.approximant_lesson: periodic substitution approximants have exact finite cycles, but their seam defects do not turn them into periodic points of X_TM
progress_and_boundary.progress: isolates a minimal uniformly recurrent nonperiodic system whose rich finite language supplies no primitive periodic-orbit source at all
progress_and_boundary.route_a_obstruction: recurrence and finite-language richness alone do not imply an intrinsic primitive-orbit layer

source_lock.allowed_data: the frozen substitution and computations derived from it
source_lock.cutoff: none in theorems; block widths <=16, approximants k<=12, and periods <=32 are replay sentinels
source_lock.forbidden_data: external prime or zero tables, arithmetic/local factors, root numbers, automorphy claims, and Route-B inputs
source_lock.normalization: Fix(n) counts points fixed by the nth power of the left shift; primitive cycles are geometric shift orbits
source_lock.object: the two-sided Thue--Morse substitution subshift X_TM generated by sigma(0)=01 and sigma(1)=10
source_lock.precision: exact binary words and exact integer counts

structural_theorems.fixed_point_recurrence: t_(2m)=t_m and t_(2m+1)=1-t_m, equivalently t_n is binary digit-sum parity
structural_theorems.minimality: uniform recurrence implies every point of X_TM has the complete Thue--Morse language, so every shift orbit meets every nonempty cylinder
structural_theorems.no_constant_triples: each pair t_(2m),t_(2m+1) is complementary, hence neither 000 nor 111 occurs
structural_theorems.uniform_recurrence: every factor u contained in w_q occurs in every t-window of length at least 4*2^q; aligned q-blocks are w_q or complement(w_q), and among any three types at least one is w_q
